Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced a GSMA mAccess Diagnostic Tool aggregation (digitaldevelopment.org) recording an 'International bandwidth per user' figure of 12.73 for Comoros, which would fall in the Low (5-19 kbit/s) band if the unit is kbit/s. However this is a single secondary aggregator, not a primary ITU/TeleGeography dataset, its vintage is unclear (the same page cites an ITU IDI country rank, an index last published in 2017), and the unit is not stated on the page. Comoros is served by the FLY-LION3 submarine cable (landed 2019, Moroni), but no primary source giving current bandwidth-per-user was found. Not confident enough to assert a non-zero code from this alone; flagged for human review rather than upgraded.
revised_comments: A single non-primary aggregator (GSMA mAccess Diagnostic Tool) records international bandwidth of approximately 12.7 (unit unstated, likely kbit/s) per internet user for Comoros, which is served by the FLY-LION3 submarine cable landing at Moroni since 2019; the vintage and unit of this figure could not be corroborated against a primary ITU or TeleGeography dataset, so it should be treated as indicative only.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced authoritative World Bank and GEF/UNDP project documentation, moving this row to the full path. The World Bank's Comoros Solar Energy Access Project appraisal (2022) records a 2018 Power Sector Master Plan setting a renewable-generation target (16% to 30% by 2033), a first grid code, and standard power purchase agreements for independent power producers, but states implementation of these reforms 'has been stalling' due to unclear institutional/regulatory structure. The Africa Minigrids Programme (AMP) Comoros national child project (UNDP/GEF, stakeholder plan dated April 2025) is actively developing a minigrid delivery model and 'appropriate policies and regulations' for off-grid investment, and its own stakeholder engagement plan states that at the time of writing there were 'no legally binding policies or explicit regulations in Comoros' on the matters it covers. This is consistent with a basic/partial policy framework (national master plan and targets exist, off-grid/mini-grid-specific regulation is still emerging) with donor-led pilot deployment rather than a comprehensive enacted framework, i.e. scale code 2. Recommend a light human check given the score sits close to the boundary with code 1.
revised_comments: Comoros' 2018 Power Sector Master Plan sets a target to raise the renewable energy share of generation from 16% to 30% by 2033, and the country has adopted a first grid code and standard power purchase agreements for independent power producers, though implementation has stalled owing to unclear institutional and regulatory arrangements. Dedicated off-grid and distributed energy deployment is being advanced mainly through donor-funded pilots, including the Africa Minigrids Programme (UNDP/GEF), which from 2025 is developing mini-grids on Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli and formulating accompanying regulations, alongside World Bank- and AfDB-supported solar PV and battery storage projects; a dedicated, legally binding off-grid/mini-grid regulatory framework has not yet been adopted.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced authoritative and convergent evidence, moving this row to the full path. The World Bank's Comoros Solar Energy Access Project appraisal (2022) describes 'increasingly long and frequent power cuts' and deteriorating service quality; the Climate Technology Centre & Network project brief (2023) describes an 'aging, unconnected power system' with supply that is 'unreliable with frequent outages, especially in rural areas' despite ~76% access; and the Africa Minigrids Programme Comoros stakeholder plan (2025) again cites 'frequent load shedding, high transmission losses'. These independent, authoritative sources from 2022-2025 consistently describe frequent/regular outages, supporting scale code 1 (Severe: frequent daily outages or regular load shedding). No World Bank Enterprise Survey quantitative outage-per-month figure for Comoros (a 2025 survey exists per the microdata catalog) could be retrieved to pin down an exact monthly count, so the qualitative multi-source corroboration is the basis for the code.
revised_comments: World Bank, Climate Technology Centre & Network and UNDP/GEF assessments from 2022-2025 consistently describe frequent and prolonged power outages across the Comorian islands, driven by an ageing and poorly interconnected grid, high transmission losses and regular load shedding; while overall electricity access averages around three-quarters of the population, supply quality is described as unreliable, with disruption most severe in rural areas.

Definition: The country's performance on the WIPO Global Innovation Index (GII), which measures innovation capabilities across institutions, human capital, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication, knowledge outputs, and creative outputs. Provides a composite view of the national innovation ecosystem.

revision_notes: Fetched the cited WIPO GII 2024 results page and cross-checked the economy profiles page: the GII 2024 covers exactly 133 economies, and Comoros is not among the listed economies (confirmed indirectly via TheGlobalEconomy.com, which shows WIPO/Cornell/INSEAD GII data for Comoros only up to 2020, with no 2024 figure). This matches the scale's own definition of code 0 ('Unknown or n.a. (not included in GII)'), so the original score is confirmed rather than changed. Year updated to 2024 to reflect the vintage of the confirming source.
revised_comments: Comoros is not among the 133 economies ranked in the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2024, so no current GII score or rank is available for the country; it last appeared with a score in the 2020 edition.
